A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Super-Linear by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original zero-shot and full-shot forecasting results, synthetic frequency experiments, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and reports additional frequency-selection, timing, and robustness comparisons.

M1.justification: The architecture, gating, and two-stage training are retained. However, Algorithm 1 changes the assignment to score in v1 into an assignment to the scale variable s in v2 line 17, while subsequently testing score. This introduces a procedural error in the written algorithm; the PDFs do not establish that the evaluated implementation changed.

E1.justification: The resampling scenarios change from ETT/Electricity cases including 45-minute, 12-hour, and daily sampling to ETTm1/2 at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 minutes. The main training and benchmark datasets remain unchanged. BizItObs at 10-second resolution was already included in v1's GIFT-Eval dataset listing.

E2.justification: V2 adds TiRex to GIFT-Eval and other comparisons. The resampling comparison removes Chronos, adds TiRex, and replaces TimesFM with TimesFM-2.0. The timing comparison substantially expands its comparator set to include TTM-R2, Chronos-Bolt variants, TimesFM-2.0, VisionTS, Sundial, and TiRex.

E3.justification: The new frequency-choice ablation selects 37 random or uniformly spaced frequencies from [1/512, 1/4], retaining the training pipeline. V2 also replaces the resampling experiment's 'only upsampling' description with resampling ETTm across the revised minute-scale grid. Main splits and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; rerunning retained comparisons is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 adds a controlled comparison of natural, random, and uniformly spaced expert frequencies, directly testing the frequency-selection premise. Appendix B.8 adds a focused analysis of BizItObs frequencies outside the experts' range, and the main resampling robustness test is revised. Earlier component, top-k, complementary-expert, and lookback analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed full-shot averaging and standard-deviation reporting are retained, including v1 Table 7 becoming v2 Table 8. The additions introduce no new reported uncertainty-estimation procedures, significance tests, or changes in run counts.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1 and 4–6 retain their forecasting scores. V2 adds TiRex's 0.716 GIFT-Eval MASE, frequency-choice and BizItObs results, and explicit latencies, including 0.0018 seconds for Super-Linear. Resampling results and comparator values change under a revised comparison. Section 4.2 also corrects LTSF best-result counts from 13/16 to 17/19, matching the unchanged Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds the analytical runtime relation T1 = Texpert/c, relating stage-one time to per-expert time and GPU count. The forecasting error bound, periodicity assumptions, and appendix proof remain unchanged. Removing the batch dimension from the model equations is equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract softens 'matches state-of-the-art performance' to demonstrating strong performance across benchmarks. The central contribution of an efficient, interpretable, frequency-specialized linear MoE for zero-shot and full-shot forecasting, and the conclusion's scope, are retained.

C2.justification: V2 attributes poorer random/uniform frequency-selection results to increased frequency approximation error and interprets BizItObs results as evidence of generalization beyond the experts' frequency range. These extend the mechanism and applicability discussion. The existing limitations concerning nonlinearity, long contexts, and uncommon frequencies are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds training-time measurements of approximately 0.72 hours per expert and 1.17 hours for stage two, a worked resampling example, and timing-test settings of lookback 512, horizon 32, and batch size 64. Hyperparameters and code access remain unchanged. Figure 5's GIFT-Eval snapshot date is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Auer et al. (2025) and a TiRex description. Section 2 more explicitly distinguishes Super-Linear's single linear-expert MoE layer from earlier methods using intermediate nonlinear modules. The remaining related-work coverage is largely retained.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized clarification of forecasting settings and single-series notation. V2 reorders the GIFT-Eval and LTSF discussion, adds an inference-time subsection and appendix subsections, and updates author formatting and wording. This is limited narrative reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the main text from two columns to one and changes typography and float placement. It merges v1 Tables 2–3 into Table 2 and Figures 7–8 into Figure 7, expands Figure 1, updates Figure 5, and adds new tables. The merged Table 2 caption reverses its left/right descriptions.

improvement.justification: The frequency-choice control, updated comparators, and explicit timing evidence better support the design and efficiency claims, while the abstract becomes more measured. These provide a modest net improvement despite new documentation errors: Algorithm 1 confuses s with score, and Table 10's prose incorrectly describes 2.05 as lower than TiRex's 1.79 and Sundial's 1.93.
